## Notes for faculty

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Two scheduling risks flagged during site build

**1. `ggplot2` before R fundamentals.** On Day 1, the first R teaching block
(11:15) goes straight to `ggplot2`, but the 12:00 hands-on block also expects
participants to cover "primers, file and project management", content that
no session formally teaches. Beginners will be asked to write
`ggplot(data, aes(...))` before they know what a data frame or a working
directory is.

*Mitigation adopted on this site:* the Prelude carries a self-paced
[R primer](prelude/r-primer.qmd) (objects, vectors, data frames, packages)
and a [project management](prelude/install.qmd#projects) walkthrough, both
sent a week ahead. Session 2 (Arun, 10:15) opens with a 10-minute
project-structure demo so nobody arrives at 11:15 cold.

**2. Day 2 afternoon is tight.** Generative AI (45 min) → live coding
(30 min) → group activity (45 min) → presentations (45 min) leaves no slack.
If the group activity is to produce a rendered Quarto document, groups need
their datasets and a template pre-loaded before lunch, not at 15:15.

*Mitigation adopted:* the [group activity brief](day2/s10-group-activity.qmd)
and starter `.qmd` are published on this site and should be handed out at the
Day 2 morning recap.
:::
